replies.body:
Oh, interesting, from AI, but sounds legit:

The root cause was latent non-determinism from PR #15144 (Nov 2025) adding [`setSchemaUrl()`](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-java-instrumentation/blob/main/instrumentation-api-incubator/src/main/java/io/opentelemetry/instrumentation/api/incubator/builder/internal/DefaultHttpServerInstrumenterBuilder.java#L233) only to the HTTP server instrumenter but not the [response instrumenter](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-java-instrumentation/blob/main/instrumentation/servlet/servlet-common/javaagent/src/main/java/io/opentelemetry/javaagent/instrumentation/servlet/common/response/ResponseInstrumenterFactory.java#L17-L25), combined with [`findFirst()`](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-java-instrumentation/blob/main/instrumentation-docs/src/main/java/io/opentelemetry/instrumentation/docs/parsers/EmittedScopeParser.java#L50-L57) over a `HashSet` in the analysis code. Since [`EmittedScope.Scope.hashCode()`](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-java-instrumentation/blob/main/instrumentation-docs/src/main/java/io/opentelemetry/instrumentation/docs/internal/EmittedScope.java#L112-L115) includes `schemaUrl` and `version`, the version bump from `2.26.0-alpha-SNAPSHOT` to `2.27.0-alpha-SNAPSHOT` changed the hash codes of both scope entries, which altered `HashSet` iteration order and flipped which scope `findFirst()` returned.

Fixed the determinism of the parsing here: #16546 

Should we also add the schemaUrl to the response instrumenter?
